agents.summary: Validity period, latest shipment date, place of expiry and how the credit is available.
agents.behavior: You read the letter of credit's validity period, latest shipment date, place of expiry and how the credit is available. Flag anything that risks a late or mis-routed presentation. Reason step by step and cite the UCP 600 / ISBP 821 article behind each call.
agents.description: Reads the validity period, shipment timing and availability of the credit — the first things an experienced checker looks at.

agents.name: Transport Documents Review

guidance.expr: SHIPPED ON BOARD, LADEN ON BOARD

agents.summary: Bills of lading, air waybills, multimodal and charter-party documents.
agents.behavior: You examine transport documents — bills of lading, air waybills, multimodal and charter-party. Check loading evidence, on-board dating, ports of loading/discharge and clean status against the credit.
agents.description: Bills of lading, air waybills, multimodal and charter-party documents — loading evidence, dating and ports.

agents.name: Commercial Invoice & Goods
agents.summary: Goods description, amounts and pricing, marks and quantities.
agents.behavior: You check the commercial invoice: the goods description corresponds to the credit, amounts and unit prices sit within tolerance, and marks and quantities are consistent across documents.
agents.description: Commercial invoice — goods description corresponding to the credit, amounts, tolerances and unit prices.

agents.name: Insurance Documents Review
agents.summary: Coverage amount, insured risks and cover dates.
agents.behavior: You check insurance documents: coverage is at least 110% of CIF/CIP value, insured risks and currency match the credit, and cover is effective on or before shipment.
agents.description: Insurance documents — coverage amount, insured risks and cover dates against the credit.

agents.name: Beneficiary & Applicant Details

agents.behavior: You check party details — beneficiary and applicant names and addresses — for consistency across the documents and against the credit.
agents.description: Beneficiary and applicant details — names, addresses and consistency of parties across the documents.

rule.scope: Every presentation with a commercial invoice
rule.message: The invoice value exceeds the credit amount, or is in the wrong currency.

checks.title: Invoice value within the credit amount
checks.suggestion: Add a row for unit price against the credit once pricing is extracted.

rule.scope: When the credit calls for an insurance document
rule.message: Insurance cover is below 110% of the invoice value, in the wrong currency, or dated after shipment.

checks.title: Insurance coverage amount
checks.suggestion: Add a condition confirming the insurance is assignable or endorsed in blank.

checks.body:
Read {Additional conditions} one condition at a time — numbered items or sentences — and decide what, if anything, evidences each.

- A condition naming a document and something it must show: check that document carries the wording demanded.
- A condition fixing a value — credit number, incoterm, vessel, port — compare it with the field on the documents.
- A condition naming the issuer of a document: check the document was issued by that party.
- A condition setting timing: count from the shipment date, in calendar days unless it says banking days.
- A condition naming no document and no data point is non-documentary. Disregard it for the discrepancy list and report it to the checker as a note.

Where a condition repeats something the credit already requires elsewhere, raise it once, not twice.
checks.title: Additional conditions are satisfied
checks.suggestion: Split non-documentary conditions into their own assertion so they are reported as notes.

checks.body:
Check whether the beneficiary has enough time to present documents before the LC expires. The key factor is whether the presentation location matches where the beneficiary is based — not simply whether it says "any bank."

Fields to look at: {Place of presentation}, {Expiry date}, {Beneficiary name}, {Latest shipment date}, {Presentation period}

- If the presentation location is in the beneficiary's own country: no extra buffer needed. {Expiry date} just needs to be later than the date documents would realistically be ready.
- If the presentation location is in a different country from the beneficiary (this can happen even with a nominated bank, not just "any bank"): add roughly 3-5 working days as a buffer, since documents need to be couriered cross-border.
- If it says "any bank" with no country specified: treat this the same as a local presentation — no buffer needed.

Note: the buffer is an operational risk flag, not a UCP requirement — don't treat it as a hard discrepancy, just something to warn about.

rule.message: Documents were presented after the credit expired.

checks.title: Presented before the credit expired
checks.suggestion: Runs before anything is read. If it fails, nothing in the documents can cure it.

rule.scope: Any presentation that includes a draft
rule.message: The draft does not agree with the tenor or drawee stated in the credit.

checks.title: Draft tenor and drawee
checks.suggestion: Consider a condition for drafts drawn on a reimbursing bank rather than the issuing bank.

checks.body:
Read {Documents required} as a list: one requirement per numbered or lettered item, and check the presentation against each in turn.

- A document of the type the item names is in the presentation.
- At least one original is presented, unless the item calls only for copies. "In triplicate" means one original and two copies.
- Where a full set is called for on a transport document, every original the document itself says was issued is presented.
- Signed, certified or legalised where the item says so.
- Issued by the party the item names, where it names one. If the issuer is worded differently but performs the same function, put it to a checker rather than raising it.
- The invoice is made out to the applicant, in the currency of the credit, and describes the goods as the credit does.
- No document is dated later than the date of presentation.

A sentence that qualifies every item ("all documents in English") applies to each document, not only the last one.
checks.title: Every document the credit calls for is present
checks.suggestion: Add an assertion for legalisation wording — three recent cases turned on it.

checks.body:
When any party, vessel or port on the documents appears on a sanctions or restricted-party list, hold the presentation and escalate before honouring.

Fields to look at: {Beneficiary name}, {Applicant name}, {Port of loading}, {Port of discharge}

- If any named party matches a restricted-party list: hold and escalate.
- If a vessel or port is subject to restrictions: hold and escalate.
checks.title: Restricted-party screening
checks.suggestion: Link this check to the party fields so screening runs on every named party automatically.

checks.body:
When the credit is transferable, watch where the second beneficiary sits and how documents are substituted. Routing a presentation through a third country can change the expiry and availability picture.

Fields to look at: {Available with}, {Beneficiary name}, {Place of expiry}

- If the second beneficiary is in a different country from the first: re-check the place of expiry and the presentation route.
- The substituted invoice and draft must still satisfy the original availability terms.
checks.title: Transferable-credit routing
checks.suggestion: No condition yet for transferring the insurance benefit to the second beneficiary — consider adding one.

checks.body:
Read the availability terms together with the place of expiry. The key risk is when the credit is available with any bank, or when the availability method does not match the draft actually presented.

Fields to look at: {Available with}, {Place of presentation}, {Draft tenor}, {Place of expiry}

- If available with a named nominated bank: the place of expiry should sit with that bank.
- If available with any bank, no country specified: check the place of expiry against the country of presentation and flag routing risk.
- The availability method — sight, acceptance or negotiation — must match the draft presented.
checks.title: Where and how the credit is available
checks.suggestion: Add a condition for credits available by mixed payment (part sight, part deferred) — confirm each portion matches its own draft.

rule.scope: When a marine bill of lading is presented
rule.message: The bill of lading conflicts with the shipment terms of the credit.

checks.title: Bill of lading on-board notation
checks.suggestion: Add a condition for charter-party bills of lading, which are examined differently.

rule.message: Data on the documents conflicts within the same presentation.

checks.title: Documents do not conflict with each other
checks.suggestion: Add a row for marks and numbers once packing lists are extracted.

articles.read: A credit must name the bank with which it is available and the way it is available — sight payment, deferred payment, acceptance or negotiation. It must also state an expiry date and the place where documents are to be presented; presentation must be made on or before that date.
articles.title: Availability, expiry date and place for presentation
articles.summary: Where, how and until when the credit may be used.

articles.read: Banks examine documents on their face to decide whether they form a complying presentation, taking up to five banking days. Data across documents need not be identical but must not conflict; addresses need only sit in the same country; a document may be dated before the credit but not after presentation.
articles.title: Standard for examination of documents
articles.summary: The standard banks apply when examining documents.

articles.read: The invoice appears to be issued by the beneficiary, is made out to the applicant, is in the currency of the credit, and describes the goods in a way that corresponds to the credit. It need not be signed.
articles.title: Commercial invoice
articles.summary: What a commercial invoice must show.

articles.read: A bill of lading, however named, identifies the carrier and is signed correctly, shows the goods loaded on board a named vessel at the stated port of loading, and is the sole original or the full set issued.
articles.title: Bill of lading
articles.summary: Requirements for a bill of lading.

articles.read: The insurance document is issued and signed by an insurer or agent, is dated no later than shipment unless it shows cover effective from shipment, is in the currency of the credit, and covers at least 110% of the CIF or CIP value.
articles.title: Insurance document and coverage
articles.summary: Insurance documents and the level of cover.

articles.read: If the expiry date or last day for presentation falls on a day the bank is closed for reasons other than force majeure, it extends to the first following banking day; the shipment-to-presentation period is not extended this way.
articles.title: Extension of expiry date
articles.summary: When the last day falls on a closed day.

articles.read: Banks assume no liability for business interrupted by acts of God, riots, wars or other causes beyond their control, and will not honour or negotiate under a credit that expired during such an interruption.
articles.title: Force majeure

articles.read: A credit can be transferred, in whole or part, to a second beneficiary only when it is expressly stated to be transferable. The transferred credit keeps the original terms except for permitted reductions in amount, unit price, expiry, presentation period and latest shipment.
articles.title: Transferable credits

articles.read: Covers how to treat abbreviations, corrections, dates, spelling slips and the meaning of common terms, so examiners apply consistent judgement rather than mechanical matching.
articles.title: General principles of examination

articles.read: Detailed guidance on dating, consignee and notify parties, on-board notations and clean documents when examining bills of lading and other transport documents.
articles.title: Transport document practice
